t.1.171.1: Aurva said: O Fathers, the vow that I then made in anger, for the destruction of all the worlds, that vow of mine must not become false.
t.1.171.3: For the man who would forgive an anger that has arisen for good cause is not able to protect properly the three aims of life.
t.1.171.2: For if the vow I made in wrath proves vain, I cannot bear to live; wrath left unfulfilled would burn me up as fire burns the kindling-stick.
t.1.171.4: For the restrainer of the unruly is the protector of the well-behaved; anger should be employed in its proper place by kings who seek to win heaven.
t.1.171.5: Then, while I lay in the womb, dwelling in my mother's thigh, I heard the wailing of the mothers when the Bhṛgus were being slaughtered by the Kṣatriyas.
t.1.171.6: When the worlds together with the immortals tolerated the extermination of the Bhṛgus, down to the very embryos, by the vilest of kṣatriyas, then wrath entered me.
t.1.171.7: My mothers, it is said, with their wombs full, and my fathers likewise, found no refuge anywhere in all the worlds because of their fear.
t.1.171.9: For when there exists in the worlds one who restrains evil, then in all the worlds no evildoer arises.
t.1.171.8: When at that time no one came to the aid of those wives of the Bhṛgus, then this fair lady carried me in one of her thighs.
t.1.171.10: But when the evildoer finds no one anywhere to restrain him, then many in the world persist in evil deeds.
t.1.171.13: Therefore, though I am angry and am today the master of these worlds, I am not able to transgress your word.
t.1.171.12: If my fathers could not be rescued by the kings and the lords, capable though they were, because they held their own lives dear in this world,
t.1.171.15: And this fire of mine, born of my wrath, which seeks to seize the worlds, would, if held back, burn me myself with its own fiery energy.
t.1.171.14: And for me too, being a lord with power, if I were to look on with indifference, there would again arise this great fear on account of the sin of the worlds.
t.1.171.16: And I know that you, sirs, desire the welfare of all the worlds; therefore, O lords, ordain what is best for the worlds and for me.
t.1.171.17: This fire born of your wrath, which seeks to seize the worlds, release it into the waters, blessings upon you, for the worlds are established in the waters.
t.1.171.18: All the essences are made of water, and the whole world is made of water; therefore, O best of the twice-born, release this fire of your wrath into the waters.
t.1.171.19: If you wish it, O Brahmin, let this fire born of your wrath dwell in the great ocean, burning the waters, for the worlds are held to be made of water.
t.1.171.11: He who, though knowing of an evil deed and having the power to do so, does not restrain it, even though he is its master, is himself bound up with that very deed.
t.1.171.20: In this way, O sinless one, this vow of yours will be fulfilled, and the worlds together with the immortals will not go to ruin.
t.1.171.21: Then, my son, Aurva released that fire born of his wrath into the abode of Varuṇa, and it consumes the waters in the great ocean.
t.1.171.23: Therefore you too, blessings be upon you, ought not to destroy the worlds, O Parāśara, best of the wise, since you know the highest dharmas.
t.1.171.22: Having become the great Horse's Head, that which the knowers of the Veda know, it spews that fire from its mouth and drinks the waters in the great ocean.
